open_questions.topic: Two cart entry points in the header with an undefined relationship
open_questions.detail: The header has a plain text NavLink labeled 'Cart' (node 6:18) inside nav-links, and a separate icon+count CartButton (node 6:22) inside header-cart on the far right. The frame does not indicate whether both point to the same destination, or one opens a mini-cart drawer while the other navigates to a full cart page.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Both are wired to the same cart destination: the icon CartButton is the primary, always-visible affordance with a live item-count; the text 'Cart' NavLink is a secondary, equivalent entry point.

options.label: Both link to the same cart view — text NavLink is a secondary/redundant affordance (assumed)
Icon CartButton opens a quick mini-cart drawer; text NavLink navigates to a separate full-page /cart

open_questions.topic: Inconsistent photography style across the Popular Pizzas grid
open_questions.detail: Node 6:86 (Classic Margherita card image) is a wide environmental restaurant shot with blurred diners in the background, while the other three card images (6:62 Diavola, 6:74 Funghi Selvatici, 6:98 Prosciutto Crudo) are close, top-down, plate-only shots. All four share the same painted box (302x220, 1.37 aspect) matching the source assets' own aspect ratio, so object-fit: cover will not mis-crop any of them — the inconsistency is purely stylistic/content, not a layout defect.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Ship all four exported source assets exactly as named in figma-assets.json without substitution, since they are the original uploads and the source of truth for this mapping.

open_questions.topic: No hover/pressed/added/disabled states drawn for the Add to Order button
open_questions.detail: Every PizzaCard's 'Add to Order' button is only shown in its default/rest visual state. The header cart badge already shows a non-zero count (3), implying an add-to-cart flow exists, but no confirmation ('Added ✓'), loading, or sold-out/disabled state is drawn anywhere in the frame.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement only the rest state exactly as drawn now; add conventional hover/pressed affordances and a lightweight transient 'Added' confirmation in code, pending a future design pass to confirm the exact visual treatment.

open_questions.topic: No design for a pizza count other than exactly 4, or for zero results
open_questions.detail: featured-grid (6:59) is a fixed 4-column row with exactly 4 PizzaCards and no pagination, 'view more' affordance scoped to the grid itself, wrap-to-second-row treatment, or empty state if the 'popular pizzas' list is ever empty (e.g., all featured items out of stock).
open_questions.arc_assumption: Build PizzaCardGrid as a responsive grid/wrap container that can hold any number of cards (not hard-coded to 4) and rely on the hero's existing 'Explore Full Menu' CTA as the sole path to the rest of the menu; no dedicated empty state is built pending confirmation.

open_questions.topic: Longer pizza names leave little room in the fixed name/price row before wrapping
open_questions.detail: 'Funghi Selvatici & Tartufo' (6:77) and 'Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola' (6:101) are both ~201px wide inside a 262px-wide row shared with the price, close to the point of wrapping or colliding with the price on narrower renders or with even slightly longer names.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Allow the pizza name to wrap to a second line above the price rather than truncate with an ellipsis, keeping price pinned to the top-right of the row.

open_questions.topic: Header ETA text and cart item count are hard-coded sample values
open_questions.detail: 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins' and the cart count '3' are static content in the Figma frame, with no empty-cart (0 items) treatment shown for the CartButton.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treat both as dynamic values sourced from app state; the Figma numbers are sample content only. Hide or zero-state the CartButton's count when the cart has 0 items, pending confirmation of the exact empty-cart visual.

open_questions.topic: Two very close warm-white background colors extracted from the frame
open_questions.detail: tokens.colors includes both #FCFAF6 (home-page canvas background, used behind the header/hero/featured/footer sections) and #F3EFE9 (story-section background only) — roughly a 2% lightness difference, seemingly used to create subtle section separation without a visible border or shadow.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Keep both as distinct tokens (--bg for the page canvas and --surface-alt for the story section) and apply them exactly where the frame does, rather than collapsing them into a single background value.
